methods.name: Stage-Progression

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Mariana Minerals is a Series A-stage climate and energy company founded by Turner Caldwell that has raised $95M+ to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comp universe of 9 peers in the Climate & Energy sector, including one public company (LNZA) and eight private firms such as Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables; the narrow filters yielded fewer than three datapoints despite the broader Climate & Energy sector containing eight peers. The stage-progression method was therefore employed as the primary valuation technique. Using the $95M total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to next-stage step-ups, this method implies a valuation of $190M.

The triangulation analysis, constrained to a single applicable method, supports a range of $162M (low) to $218M (high), with a median of $190M. Key uncertainties include the lack of granular same-stage peer data to validate the stage multiplier assumption and the heterogeneity within Climate & Energy subsectors, which limits the precision of any sector-wide benchmark. A more robust estimate would require either closer-stage comparables or additional methodological anchors.
